name: Nachos
reason: Replace the implausible two-chip amount with an explicit editorial serving basis.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Spread 150 g tortilla chips in a single layer on a baking tray.
Grate the cheddar and Monterey Jack and scatter both evenly over the chips.
Add the sliced jalapeños and bake for 8–10 minutes, until the cheese has melted.
Divide into 3 portions and serve immediately with the measured salsa, sour cream and guacamole.

name: Croissant
reason: Define a small-batch dough, separate dough and lamination butter, and include egg wash.
ingredients: 20 g for the dough; 80 g for lamination
beaten whole egg; amount used for brushing
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, milk, sugar, salt and 20 g softened butter into a smooth dough. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Flatten the remaining 80 g cold butter between sheets of baking paper into a small square. Chill until firm but pliable.
Roll the dough around the butter to enclose it. Roll into a rectangle and fold in thirds. Chill for 30 minutes. Repeat the rolling, folding and chilling 3 more times, keeping the butter cold.
Roll the dough about 4 mm thick and cut into 6 long triangles. Roll each triangle from its base to its tip and place on a lined baking tray.
Leave to proof for about 2 hours at room temperature, until visibly puffy. The butter should not melt during proofing.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Brush with 10 g beaten egg and bake for 15–18 minutes, until deeply golden. Makes 6 small croissants.

name: Apple Pie
reason: Choose one pastry method instead of counting ready-made pastry and incomplete homemade pastry together; add egg wash and define the filling.
ingredients: ready-made pastry for a base and lid
80 g for filling; 10 g for topping
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Divide the ready-made pastry in half. Roll one half to line a 23 cm pie dish and keep the other half chilled for the lid.
Slice the peeled, cored apples. Toss with 80 g sugar, cinnamon, 20 g flour and lemon juice.
Spoon the filling into the pastry case and dot with the 20 g butter.
Roll out the remaining pastry, cover the pie and seal the edges. Cut several steam vents in the lid.
Brush with 15 g beaten egg and sprinkle with the remaining 10 g sugar.
Bake for 20 minutes at 200°C, then reduce to 175°C and bake for another 35–40 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Cool for about 2 hours before cutting into 8 slices.

name: French Mushroom Omelette
reason: Resolve the two-versus-three egg conflict, reduce the contradictory teaspoon of salt, and allocate butter between the two cooking steps.
ingredients: 10 g for mushrooms; 5 g for eggs
steps: Slice the mushrooms and cook in 10 g butter until golden and their moisture has evaporated. Set aside.
Whisk the 3 eggs with 0.5 g salt until uniform.
Melt the remaining 5 g butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour in the eggs.
Gently draw the set egg from the edges towards the centre while tilting the pan so the uncooked egg fills the gaps.
When the surface is almost set, add the mushrooms, grated Gruyère and chopped chives to one half.
Fold the omelette in half and slide onto a plate. Serve immediately.

name: Mushroom Omelette
reason: Resolve the egg and salt contradictions and choose a specified cheese for a reproducible recipe.
ingredients: 10 g for mushrooms; 5 g for eggs
steps: Slice the mushrooms and cook in 10 g butter over medium-high heat until golden and their moisture has evaporated. Set aside.
Whisk the 3 eggs with the measured salt and pepper.
Melt the remaining 5 g butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat and pour in the eggs.
Gently draw the set egg towards the centre while tilting the pan to fill the gaps with uncooked egg.
When almost set, add the mushrooms, grated cheddar and chopped chives to one half. Fold over and serve immediately.

name: Double Smash Burger
reason: Make two 90 g patties and one double burger agree with the ingredient quantities; specify onion and butter rather than an unexplained prepared component.
steps: Thinly slice the onion and cook in 5 g butter over low heat for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden. Add a splash of water if it begins to catch.
Divide the 180 g beef into two loose 90 g balls without compacting them.
Heat a cast-iron pan until very hot. Add the beef balls, spaced apart, and press each firmly into a thin patty.
Season with the measured salt and pepper. Cook until the underside is well browned, about 90 seconds.
Flip each patty, add one slice of cheese and continue cooking until the beef is cooked through.
Toast the split bun. Spread with the sauce and stack both patties, the cooked onion and sliced pickles inside the single bun.
